housing.summary: Rome's rental market is competitive, especially in central rioni (Centro Storico, Trastevere, Prati). Long-term leases (contratto di locazione) typically run 4+4 years; furnished short/medium-term options are common for relocating employees. A landlord usually requires proof of income, ID/codice fiscale, and often a guarantor. Idealista, Immobiliare.it and agency listings dominate the market.

banking.summary: Opening a resident bank account (conto corrente) requires a codice fiscale, valid ID/passport, and proof of address; residence registration helps. Major retail banks include Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, BPER and BNL, alongside digital options. Non-residents can open a conto non residente with more limited features until residency is established.
banking.required_docs: Codice fiscale, valid passport/ID, proof of address

schools.summary: Rome has a broad range of international and bilingual schools serving relocating families, offering British, American and IB curricula, plus French, German and other national systems. Places at popular international schools can be limited, so early application is advised. Italian state schools follow the national curriculum in Italian.
schools.curricula: British, American, IB, French, German, Italian national

legal_admin.summary: EU/EEA nationals staying beyond 3 months register their residence (residenza) with the Comune di Roma anagrafe; non-EU nationals must first obtain a permesso di soggiorno via the Questura/post office kit and then register residence. The codice fiscale is needed for almost all administrative steps.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register residence (iscrizione anagrafica / residenza) at the Comune di Roma anagrafe

tax_finance.summary: The codice fiscale is the Italian tax identification code, required for employment, banking, renting and most contracts; it is issued by the Agenzia delle Entrate. Tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; special regimes (e.g. impatriati / inbound worker relief) may apply to qualifying relocating employees.

transport.summary: Rome's public transport is run by ATAC and includes three metro lines (A, B/B1, C), extensive buses, trams and urban rail, integrated under the Metrebus ticketing system. A monthly pass covers metro, bus and tram within the city. Non-EU licence holders must generally exchange or re-sit for an Italian licence, while EU/EEA licences are broadly valid; healthcare access is via registration with the local ASL for the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences valid; non-EU licences generally require exchange or re-testing (conversione patente)
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with the local ASL to enroll in the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN) and obtain a tessera sanitaria
